body:
> Unfortunately, it doesn't seem like this can be reproduced in isolation. I tried with an MRP but the code works just fine there, both on 4.4.1 and 4.5.beta6

To be clear: the error does *not* occur in the MRP? If so we need more details to be able to do anything, please try to gradually scale your project down to get to a point where it does happen but no unnecessary content is present

Before I try duplicating the project and scaling that one down, I just noticed something

When the error happens, the debugger shows the value of the `file` var as `hn_barracks.tres`. That's the *second* file in the `"res://data/objects/refs/"` folder

So I put a print statement at the end of the for-loop, ran the scene again and, lo and behold, it printed:
```dn_weaver.tres loaded```

Meaning the code works just fine on the first resource file, but when it tries to load the next, something goes wrong

I found the cause of the issue.

One of the custom resource classes in the project is `TechTree`. In it, there's an `@export` typed dictionary with `RTSObjectRef` as the key type and `TechTreeBranch` as the value type

This was for the RTS game's tech tree system. I wanted each faction to have a default tech tree, and certain units/buildings would each have a selection of other units/buildings they could make.

This was how I went about it in code:
```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name TechTree
@export var branches: Dictionary[RTSObjectRef, TechTreeBranch]
```
```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name TechTreeBranch
@export var items: Array[TechTreeItem]
```
```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name TechTreeItem
@export var ref: RTSBaseRef
```

Thing is, using a typed dictionary like this (that's what it seems to be) gave me some trouble earlier. I'd suddenly get these errors:
```
Invalid call. Nonexistent function 'get_branch_from_ref' in base 'Resource'.
```
```
Attempted to assign an object into a TypedArray, that does not inherit from 'GDScript'.
```
When I looked through the forums and GitHub issues, I eventually found #109345, and since it seems to be somewhat on pause for now, I bandaided the issue by commenting out the logic that would call for any `TechTree` resources, and things worked fine from there

...Until this error happened. After looking a bit, I initially thought the issue was the `RTSObjectRef` resource files themselves, seeing as the ones that failed to load wouldn't show their `@export` vars in the inspector when looking at them through the debugger, so I tried deleting one and remaking it. The problem persisted

Then it turned out, that the failure to load was being caused by those resources being in the dictionary of an existing `TechTree` resource I had in the filesystem. And once I removed them from that dictionary, *the game ran properly*

Sadly I still can't get the error to happen in the MRP, but at least I know what was causing it

I'm going to close this. Since there is no actionable MRP attached. From reading the discussion in here, I'm convinced that this is a variation of similar cyclic loader issues. However without inspecting the full project it's not possible to know exactly where the cycle is coming from. We have other issues tracking this, which come with MRPs (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/80877).
